parakeet: What does it say about a God who can create everything to be visibly seen, measured, experienced, and shared with others except itself? Why is God the only thing believers claim explains reality while also being the hardest thing in reality to demonstrate? The Christian God is presented as the explanation for everything we can observe while being exempted from the observation itself. If a God can create stars, galaxies, mountains, oceans, DNA, gravity, consciousness, and an entire universe that can be observed, tested, measured, photographed, experienced, and independently verified by other people, why is that same God the one thing that cannot be directly demonstrated in the same way? Today I want to highlight a few underlying problems that rarely get discussed. Let's start with the asymmetry problem. Everything else in existence appears to leave detectable traces. We infer black holes because they affect surrounding matter. We infer electrons because they produce measurable effects. We infer ancient civilizations because they leave artifacts. But God is often described as exempt from the very standards of evidence used to establish the existence of everything else. That leads many non-believers to ask, why would the most important being in the universe be the least detectable? Or an even deeper question is, how can something be inferred or implied without first being detected? To infer something means to see an effect and logically trace it back to its cause, but you cannot trace an effect to a cause if the cause leaves no unique trace. When we infer a black hole, we're measuring real gravity and real light. We're detecting its impact. But when theology claims to infer God from the universe, it isn't measuring God's impact. It's looking at the universe and asserting that God did it. If an entity cannot be detected in any way, it has no relationship with reality. And if it has no relationship with reality, it cannot leave an implication. You can't be implied by a universe you're completely absent from. If something is inferred without being detected, it means the word inference has lost all its power. It's no longer a tool for discovering truth. It's just a fancy word for an unfalsifiable assumption.
